correctness.rationale: Two standalone exact finite algorithms independently enumerate all 33 perfect matchings and 6/8 exchanges, one by vertex recursion and DFS of cycles, the other by 40320 bipartite bijections and relative permutation cycle lengths. Both reconstruct all graph components, eccentricity and pair-distance distributions and verify the subdivided double-triangle model. All universes and boundaries are finite and explicitly exhaustive; no sampling is used.

evidence: Ito et al. section 1 permits any alternating cycle, and guarantees reachability in that less restrictive rule.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Unrestricted matching connectivity cannot imply connectivity at cycles bounded by 8, since requiring shorter moves removes reconfiguration edges. General hardness of fixed even-length rules does not determine this instance or the structural octagon graph. Hamilton decomposition is another configuration problem.

value.rationale: The graph is a canonical small arc-transitive cubic bipartite graph of girth six, where local alternating hexagon trades are a natural minimal available move. The theorem locates a sharp reachability threshold, identifies exactly the inaccessible matching states, and exhibits an explicit minimal octagon backbone with quantitative diameter improvement when both move types are used; this is a structurally motivated reconfiguration benchmark, not an arbitrary count.
